walkthroughs.body_html:
A Divided Union: USA 1945-70 — a core area of GCSE History.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

A Divided Union: USA 1945-70 brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with A Divided Union: USA 1945-70.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What did the Supreme Court rule in Brown v Board of Education (1954)?
options: Segregated public schools were unconstitutional
Buses across America must desegregate immediately
Literacy tests for voting were banned
Trade unions could not exclude Black workers

mcqs.q: Whose arrest sparked the Montgomery Bus Boycott in 1955?
options: Rosa Parks
Emmett Till
Coretta Scott King
Thurgood Marshall

mcqs.q: Which senator led the anti-communist accusations of the early 1950s?
options: Joseph McCarthy
John F. Kennedy
Barry Goldwater
Lyndon B. Johnson

mcqs.q: What did the Civil Rights Act of 1964 do?
options: Banned segregation in public places and discrimination in employment
Gave women the vote for the first time
Abolished slavery in the southern states
Ended the war in Vietnam

mcqs.q: Did the Montgomery Bus Boycott end segregation across America?
options: The Montgomery Bus Boycott ended segregation throughout the United States.
The Montgomery Bus Boycott was about equal pay for bus drivers.
No - it desegregated Montgomery's buses after a Supreme Court ruling and energised the movement, but wider segregation survived until the Civil Rights Act of 1964 and beyond.
Black Americans were not allowed to vote anywhere until 1970.

mcqs.q: Did Joseph McCarthy prove there were hundreds of communists in the US government?
options: The Montgomery Bus Boycott was about equal pay for bus drivers.
No - McCarthy never substantiated his shifting claims, and his bullying at the televised Army-McCarthy hearings of 1954 led the Senate to censure him.
McCarthy uncovered a vast proven network of Soviet agents inside the government.
McCarthy was the director of the FBI during the Red Scare.

mcqs.q: Did Black Americans only gain the legal right to vote in 1964?
options: Black Americans were not allowed to vote anywhere until 1970.
McCarthy was the director of the FBI during the Red Scare.
The Civil Rights Act of 1964 gave Black Americans the vote for the first time.
No - the 15th Amendment (1870) had granted Black men the vote; the problem was obstacles like literacy tests, which the Voting Rights Act of 1965 targeted.
